definition: Jais is an open-source large language model launched in August 2023.
details: Developed as a collaboration between Emirati AI company G42, the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI), and US-based Cerebras Systems, Jais was designed to produce high-quality Arabic text and was also trained on English data. The model's creation was motivated by the underrepresentation of the Arabic language in the field of generative artificial intelligence. It aims to provide a more culturally and linguistically accurate model for the world's 400 million Arabic speakers. Its name is a reference to Jebel Jais, the highest mountain in the UAE.

explainer.lead: Jais is an open-source large language model launched in August 2023 that was designed to produce high-quality Arabic text and was also trained on English data. It matters because Arabic was underrepresented in generative AI, and the model aims to serve the world's roughly 400 million Arabic speakers more accurately.

tiers.eli5: Most AI language models grew up speaking mostly English; Jais was raised to speak Arabic well too, so Arabic speakers get answers that fit their language and culture.
tiers.practitioner: Builders targeting Arabic-language applications can start from Jais rather than an English-first model. The pitfall is assuming quality carries across domains: the model was motivated by and tuned for cultural and linguistic accuracy, so evaluation should be done in the target Arabic variety.
tiers.paperLevel: Jais is an open-source large language model trained on Arabic data alongside English data, developed by G42, MBZUAI, and Cerebras Systems. Known limits: it is a 2023 release and its stated scope is Arabic and English text, not other languages.

explainer.example: A developer building an Arabic-language assistant selects Jais because it was trained to generate culturally and linguistically accurate Arabic rather than treating Arabic as a translation afterthought.
